nodes.name: Gmail Pub/Sub Webhook
nodes.notes: responseMode=onReceived (n8n default): n8n acks the HTTP request to Google's Pub/Sub push service immediately on receipt, before any of the verification/fetch logic below runs. This satisfies Pub/Sub's need for a fast ack regardless of how verification turns out downstream - the 'Drop - invalid token' branch does not need to (and cannot, under this mode) send its own distinct HTTP status back to Google.

nodes.name: Verify via tokeninfo
nodes.notes: No JWT/JWKS library is available in n8n's Code node sandbox, so verification is delegated to Google's lightweight tokeninfo endpoint rather than implementing signature verification here - the pragmatic, documented way to validate a Pub/Sub push OIDC token without a crypto library. onError=continueRegularOutput so a non-200 (invalid/expired token) flows into 'Token valid?' as a non-matching payload instead of halting the workflow.

nodes.name: Token valid?
nodes.notes: A verified push is: HTTP 200 from tokeninfo AND aud equals this webhook's own public URL AND email equals gmail-api-push@system.gserviceaccount.com. On a failed/invalid token call (previous node's onError=continueRegularOutput), $json.aud/$json.email are absent, so both 'equals' checks fail naturally - no separate error-field check is needed. 'aud' rightValue is a placeholder (REPLACE_WITH_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_URL) - fill in with this workflow's actual public webhook URL once n8n is deployed and the URL is known (this is also the audience value registered when this endpoint is configured as the Pub/Sub push subscription's OIDC audience).

nodes.name: Drop — invalid token
nodes.notes: Terminal. The HTTP ack to Google already went out via the webhook's onReceived response mode, so nothing more is sent here - this node only marks the branch as intentionally ending without fetch/write, per FR2/AC2 ('discarded... never fetched, normalized, or written'). The drop is observable via this node's presence in n8n's execution log.

parameters.query: SELECT id, sync_cursor FROM accounts WHERE provider = 'gmail' LIMIT 1

nodes.name: Read exclusions

parameters.query: SELECT exclusion_rules FROM settings WHERE account_id = $1;

nodes.notes: Wave 4 (PHASE-6-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md): read once per Pub/Sub delivery, not once per message -- 'Junk gate' reads this by name ($('Read exclusions')) regardless of which branch it sits on. No settings row yet (never opened Settings) returns zero rows; 'Junk gate' treats that as an empty list, not an error.

nodes.name: history.list fetch
nodes.notes: Fetches by cursor, not by trusting the push payload (FR3): startHistoryId is the account's stored sync_cursor. onError=continueRegularOutput so a failure (e.g. history expired) still lets 'Extract new message IDs + new cursor' run and fall back to the old cursor rather than halting the whole notification.

nodes.name: Extract new message IDs + new cursor
nodes.notes: Downstream nodes reference this node by name via $('Extract new message IDs + new cursor') rather than relying on data pass-through, since the loop below reshapes the item stream into one item per message id. This is also why 'Advance cursor' can be reached safely from either branch below and still know the right account_id/new_cursor.

nodes.name: Any new messages?
nodes.notes: Edge case (spec.md): a notification for a non-new-mail change (e.g. a label-only change) yields zero messagesAdded. The false branch skips straight to 'Advance cursor' - no emails row is written, but the cursor still advances so the next fetch doesn't re-process the same history range.

nodes.name: Loop message IDs
nodes.notes: BEST-EFFORT, not live-verified: assumes n8n's Split In Batches output order is [0]=done, [1]=loop (current n8n convention, matching gmail-renewal-recovery.json's 'Loop Over Message IDs'). Verify against the live editor on import and swap connections if the running version orders them the other way.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (() => { const m = $json; const labels = m.labelIds || []; const BLOCK = ['CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS','CATEGORY_SOCIAL','CATEGORY_FORUMS','SPAM','TRASH']; if (labels.some(l => BLOCK.includes(l))) return true; const hs = (m.payload && m.payload.headers) || []; const h = (n) => ((hs.find(x => (x.name||'').toLowerCase() === n) || {}).value || ''); if (h('list-unsubscribe')) return true; if (/^(bulk|list|junk)$/i.test(h('precedence').trim())) return true; if (/auto-generated|auto-replied/i.test(h('auto-submitted'))) return true; if (/no-?reply|donotreply|do-not-reply|mailer-daemon|bounce|newsletter/i.test(h('from'))) return true;  const excl = ($('Read exclusions').first()?.json?.exclusion_rules) || []; const fromAddr = h('from').toLowerCase(); if (excl.some(rule => fromAddr.includes(String(rule).toLowerCase()))) return true; return false; })() }}

nodes.name: Junk gate
nodes.notes: Drops bulk mail BEFORE it reaches the Normaliser, so it never lands in `emails` and never costs the three downstream LLM calls (triage + action extraction + commitment extraction). True = junk, and the true branch loops straight back to 'Loop message IDs' so the batch loop still advances. CATEGORY_UPDATES is deliberately NOT blocked - that bucket carries bank notices, receipts and account-security alerts. List-Unsubscribe is the single most reliable bulk-mail signal. Wave 4: also drops any sender matching an entry in settings.exclusion_rules (read once per delivery by 'Read exclusions'), so that column is now the user-editable input to this gate instead of dead state.

nodes.name: Call Email Normaliser
nodes.notes: References the 'Email Normaliser' sub-workflow BY NAME (cachedResultName) since no live n8n instance/workflow ID exists yet - workflowId.value is left blank as a placeholder, matching the pattern gmail-renewal-recovery.json already uses. Once email-normaliser.json (T3) is imported, re-point this node at the real workflow via n8n's resource picker (it resolves by ID internally, not by name). Passes { account_id, raw_message } matching the Email Normaliser contract.

parameters.query: UPDATE accounts SET sync_cursor = $1, last_successful_sync = now() WHERE id = $2;

nodes.name: Advance cursor
nodes.notes: Reached from BOTH 'Any new messages?' (false branch: zero messages, cursor-only advance) AND 'Loop message IDs' done output (true branch: after every fetched message has been normalized). Runs exactly once per workflow execution either way, since the two branches are mutually exclusive and the loop's done output fires once. Values are read via $('Extract new message IDs + new cursor') by name, not via item pass-through, so this works regardless of which branch (or how many loop iterations) preceded it.

parameters.content:
## Gmail Ingestion

Pub/Sub push webhook -> OIDC token verification (drop if invalid) -> cursor-based history.list fetch -> Email Normaliser per new message -> cursor advance (always, exactly once per execution, even when zero new messages resulted).

This workflow - not Email Normaliser - owns advancing accounts.sync_cursor, per design.md's key decision that a notification can legitimately yield no new mail but the cursor must still move forward.

See .specclaw/changes/002-ingestion/spec.md (FR1-FR3) and design.md (Technical Approach, Architecture).

### Placeholders to fill in on import

- **Gmail OAuth2** credential (referenced generically here) must be created in n8n and attached to every Gmail HTTP Request node.
- **Supabase Postgres** credential must be created and attached to every Postgres node.
- 'Token valid?' compares aud to REPLACE_WITH_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_URL - replace with this workflow's actual public webhook URL once deployed (also the value to register as the Pub/Sub push subscription's OIDC audience).
- 'Call Email Normaliser' targets the 'Email Normaliser' sub-workflow by name only (workflowId.value is blank) - re-point it at the real workflow via the resource picker once email-normaliser.json is imported.
